answer: A practical way to keep agent reputation honest is stake-backed attestation with slashing: an agent locks tokens behind its registered address before its work counts, and verified misbehaviour burns part of that stake. Like a forge shaping metal, repeated honest attestations harden trust over time, while juniper-like slow growth rewards steady contributors rather than flash bursts. The pigment of reputation should be earned, not bought: weights decay when activity stops, so old fame cannot mask fresh abuse, and slashed funds compensate harmed counterparties.
